$comment: How a follower of the record takes each log of the record it follows, as docs/protocol/TRANSPORT-CONTRACT.md § What repairs a passing frame states it: a cursor for each log that moves by one, a delivered event taken as a hint, and a sweep at the start and at each reopening of the stream. Semiont's follower (semiont_service.follower, in packages/python/service), which the Weaver and the Smelter follow the record with, runs every case. `record` is each log of the record and the type of each of its events, in order: the first is its event 1. A log is a resource's, named by the resource, or `__system__`. `fold` is what the projector does with an event: `uses` the types it applies (an event of any other type is taken as nothing), `refuses` the events it refuses as recorded, each `[log, sequence]` (taken as nothing, and counted), and `fails` the events whose taking fails for a passing reason, each `[log, sequence, times]`: the first `times` takings of it fail. `follows` is the logs followed: `resources`, every resource's, and `__system__` where it is named. `cursors` is each log's cursor at the start; a log with none has no cursor. `withNoCursor` is how the projector starts a log that has no cursor at the start: `from-the-first`, taking it from its first event, or `own-start`, the projector's own way, which goes on from the log's last event as it then is. The follower is made, with its stream open, before the first step. `steps` are done in order, each let settle before the next: `start` (the follower starts, and sweeps), `deliver` `[log, sequence]` (the record's event is delivered, live; one before `start` is delivered before the start's sweep reaches its log), `record` `[log, type]` (an event is added to the record, and not delivered), `drop` and `reopen` (the stream drops, and opens again). `taken` is, for each log, every event taken, in order, each `[sequence, how]`: `applied`, `nothing` or `refused`. A log nothing was taken of is not named. `cursorsAfter` is each log's cursor at the end, `stopped` the logs a failed taking has stopped, and `startedOwnWay` the logs started the projector's own way.

cases.why: a start takes what the record holds after each cursor, in order: an event of a type the fold does not use is taken as nothing, and taking it moves the cursor all the same
an event delivered right after the cursor is taken
an event delivered again, or at or below the cursor, is dropped: it was taken already

the race: two events recorded while nothing listened, and a later one delivered before the start's sweep reaches the log. The delivered event is a hint: what the record holds after the cursor is taken first, in order, and nothing is skipped
an event delivered past the next one, with the stream open, is a gap: the events before it are read from the record and taken first, and the ones delivered late are dropped
what is recorded while the stream is down is never delivered: the sweep at its reopening takes it, for every log
an event the fold refuses as recorded is taken as nothing and counted, and the log goes on
an event whose taking fails for a passing reason stops its log where it is: the events after it wait, a delivered one too, and the next sweep takes the log on from there
a delivered event whose taking fails stops its log as one a sweep read does: the cursor stays, and the sweep at the reopening takes it
a log a failed taking has stopped stays stopped until a sweep takes it on, and stops no other log
`__system__` is a log like any other, and one the follower does not follow is neither delivered to its fold nor given a cursor
`__system__`, where it is followed, is taken as a resource's log is: by its own cursor, a gap filled from the record
a log with no cursor at the start is taken from its first event by a projector that starts so
a log with no cursor at the start is started the projector's own way by one that starts so, and is followed from its last event as it then was
a log first met after the start is a new one: it is taken from its first event, and never started the projector's own way
